a.what_and_why: Bench sensor calibration teaches the compass's own sensors (magnetometer, accelerometer, and gyroscope) their individual biases and scale, on the bench, before it's mounted on the boat. Every later stage builds on this one, and heading is never transmitted until it's done.
before_you_start: Assemble the compass in its final enclosure with all cables attached -- calibrating a bare board doesn't account for the enclosure's own magnetic footprint.
Move at least 1 m away from other electronics, speakers, metal tools, and anything magnetic.
Power the compass and connect to its Wi-Fi network from your phone.

steps.title: Hold still
steps.detail: Set the compass down on a stable, non-metallic surface and leave it untouched until the app shows it's detected stillness.

steps.title: Six positions
steps.detail: Pick the compass up and hold it steady in each of six orientations in turn -- top up, bottom up, and each of the four sides -- for a few seconds each, in any order.

steps.title: Slow rotation
steps.detail: Slowly rotate the compass through as many different orientations as you can, like tracing a figure-8 in the air, until the coverage indicator fills up.

a.success_looks_like: All three sensor accuracy indicators (magnetometer, accelerometer, gyroscope) reach High, and the app confirms the calibration was saved.
if_it_fails: Stuck on Hold still: set the compass on a firmer, more stable surface -- vibration or hand tremor prevents the stillness check from passing.
Accuracy won't reach High: move further from magnetic interference (speakers, metal furniture, other electronics) and repeat the six positions and rotation steps.
Timed out: the previous saved calibration (if any) is unaffected -- just start over when ready.

b.what_and_why: Installation alignment tells the compass how it's actually mounted on the boat: whether it's perfectly level, and which way its own "forward" points relative to the boat's true bow. Without this, a perfectly-calibrated sensor still reports the wrong heading if it's mounted tilted or rotated from dead-ahead.
before_you_start: The compass must be permanently mounted in its final position -- this stage measures the actual installation, not a bench setup.
The boat should be at rest on calm water for the level step.
Know how you'll determine the boat's true bow bearing: either a known landmark/chart bearing, or by holding a steady course on GPS.

steps.title: Set level
steps.detail: With the boat at rest and calm, tap Set level and hold still for a few seconds while the compass captures its mounted attitude.

steps.title: Choose a bearing method
steps.detail: Pick Known bearing if you can sight or chart the boat's true bow direction right now, or GPS course if you'd rather hold a steady course underway and let the chartplotter's GPS provide it.

b.duration_estimate: About 5 minutes at the dock, or a few minutes underway for the GPS method
b.success_looks_like: The app shows a preview of how the displayed heading will change, and after you accept it, the mounting offset is saved.
if_it_fails: Set level won't complete: the boat is rocking too much -- wait for calmer water.
GPS course method waiting: it needs boat speed above a minimum and a steady course -- hold a straight line at a reasonable cruising speed.
Wrong-looking offset: discard and redo Set level, making sure the boat was genuinely at rest.

c.what_and_why: A compass swing measures the boat's own magnetic deviation -- the small heading error caused by the boat's engine, wiring, and metal structure, which changes with the boat's own heading. Correcting it is the last step to a fully accurate compass.
before_you_start: Stages A and B should already be done -- this stage corrects the boat's own magnetism on top of an already-calibrated, already-aligned sensor.
Find open water with room for at least two full slow circles, away from other traffic.
If your chartplotter provides GPS course over ground (COG) to the bus, the guided swing below will use it automatically; otherwise use the manual 8-point fallback.

steps.title: Guided GPS swing
steps.detail: Start the swing and steer at least two complete, slow, steady circles at a safe cruising speed, covering every heading. The coverage ring fills in as each heading direction gets enough samples.

steps.title: Manual 8-point fallback
steps.detail: If no GPS course source is available, steady the boat on each of the 8 compass points (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) in turn and enter the true reference bearing for each.

c.success_looks_like: Full sector coverage across at least two turns, with a low-residual deviation curve -- the app shows the fitted curve, max deviation, and fit quality before you accept it.
if_it_fails: Turning too fast: the app will flag it -- slow down and keep the turn rate even.
Rejected for incomplete coverage: keep turning until every heading direction has enough accepted samples across two full turns.
Rejected for high residual or deviation: strong current/wind, a magnetic disturbance, or an incomplete Stage A/B may be the cause -- redo the swing once conditions are calmer.
